intro.en: Three generations, one recipe: marrow bones simmered from the afternoon before, rice noodles made every morning, beef bought fresh that day. Open from 6 a.m.

body.en: In 1986 our grandfather carried his broth pot on a shoulder pole to the corner of Lo Duc street before dawn. Regulars called it "phở gánh" — the stall pho — and the name stuck.

body.en: Beef marrow bones simmer on a low flame from 5 p.m., skimmed constantly for a clear broth. Charred ginger and onion, cinnamon, star anise and black cardamom go in before dawn to keep their aroma.
